test_title: PYST 61: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Reserve Bank of India revised Priority Sector Lending (PSL) guidelines for Small Finance Banks from FY 2025–26, reducing the PSL target to what percentage of ANBC (adjusted net bank credit) or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposures (CEOBE)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**60%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in a notification issued in **April 2024**, announced a significant revision to the **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** targets for **Small Finance Banks (SFBs)** to bring them on par with universal banks.
 
• As per the revised guidelines, the overall **PSL target** for **Small Finance Banks**, which was previously mandated at **75%**, will be reduced in a phased manner. For the financial year **2025–26** (specifically by **March 31, 2026**), the target has been set at **60%** of **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** or **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)**, whichever is higher.
 
• The primary objective of this revision is to provide a **level playing field** for **SFBs** and to harmonize their regulatory requirements with those of **Universal Banks**, which currently have a **40%** PSL target.
 
• Before this revision, **Small Finance Banks** were required to maintain a much higher threshold of **75%** to ensure that credit reached the **unserved and underserved sections** of the population, including small farmers and micro-units.
 
• The **RBI** has implemented a **glide path** for this transition: the target remains **75%** until **March 31, 2025**; it reduces to **60%** by **March 31, 2026**; and finally reaches **40%** by **March 31, 2027**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):** It is a **regulatory framework** established by the **RBI** that mandates banks to allocate a specific portion of their **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** to certain sectors that are considered vital for the **inclusive development** of the country. These sectors include **Agriculture**, **Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**, **Export Credit**, **Education**, **Housing**, **Social Infrastructure**, and **Renewable Energy**.
 
• **Small Finance Banks (SFBs):** These are a specific category of banks established to provide **financial inclusion** to sections of the economy not being served by other banks. They are registered as **public limited companies** under the **Companies Act, 2013** and are governed by the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**. Notable examples include **AU Small Finance Bank**, **Equitas Small Finance Bank**, and **Jana Small Finance Bank**.
 
• **ANBC and CEOBE:** **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** represents the total credit provided by a bank after making specific adjustments for bills rediscounted and other prescribed exemptions. **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)** refers to the potential credit risk from non-fund-based limits like **letters of credit** or **bank guarantees**.
 
• **Regulatory Scope:** While the overall target is being reduced, **SFBs** are still required to focus on their core mission of serving **Small and Marginal Farmers** and **Weaker Sections**. The **RBI** maintains specific sub-targets within the PSL framework to ensure these vulnerable groups continue to receive adequate credit flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for SFBs:** To be eligible for a license, the **minimum paid-up voting equity capital** for **SFBs** was initially **Rs. 100 crore**, which has been increased to **Rs. 200 crore** in recent guidelines, except for those transitioned from **Urban Co-operative Banks**.
 
• **The Glide Path Schedule:**
 
 
• **75%**: Applicable up to the end of **FY 2024-25**.
 
• **60%**: Target for the end of **FY 2025-26**.
 
• **40%**: Final target to be achieved by the end of **FY 2026-27**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Revision:** This move is expected to improve the **profitability** and **operational flexibility** of **Small Finance Banks**, as they can now diversify their loan portfolios toward higher-yielding non-priority sectors as they grow in size and scale.
 
• **Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks (UCBs):** It is important to note that **UCBs** are also on a similar glide path to reach a **75%** PSL target by **March 31, 2026**, showing the **RBI's** efforts to balance different banking tiers according to their specific mandates and risks.
